name: onesixtyone - SNMP Community String Brute Force
description: Fast UDP-based SNMP community string brute forcer. Sweeps single hosts or entire subnets using a wordlist of common community strings.

variations.description: Brute community strings against single host
variations.label: onesixtyone (brute)

variations.description: Sweep entire subnet with community wordlist
variations.label: onesixtyone (brute)

variations.description: Build minimal community list from defaults then sweep
variations.command: echo public > /tmp/community && echo private >> /tmp/community && echo manager >> /tmp/community && onesixtyone -c /tmp/community <cidr>
variations.label: echo public > /tmp/community

variations.description: Use SecLists SNMP community string wordlist
variations.label: onesixtyone (brute)

variations.description: Feed targets from file (hosts with UDP 161 open)
variations.label: onesixtyone (brute)

examples.label: Brute single host with SecLists wordlist
Build defaults list and sweep /24
examples.command: echo public > /tmp/community && echo private >> /tmp/community && echo manager >> /tmp/community && onesixtyone -c /tmp/community 192.168.50.1-254

examples.label: Feed nmap SNMP host discovery output as target list
examples.command: grep 'Up' open-snmp.txt | cut -d' ' -f2 > snmp-targets.txt && onesixtyone -c /opt/useful/seclists/Discovery/SNMP/snmp.txt -i snmp-targets.txt

notes: SNMP community strings are essentially cleartext passwords for SNMPv1/v2c. 'public' (read-only) and 'private' (read-write) are present in production environments far more often than they should be. Test these two before running full brute force. Chaining: port scan confirms UDP 161 open → onesixtyone to find valid community strings → snmpwalk/snmpbulkwalk to dump full MIB → braa for bulk extended OID enumeration. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 6 (Information Gathering).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Penetration Testing with Kali Linux
MITRE ATT&CK - Brute Force: Password Spraying

recommended.note: Once valid community string found, use snmpwalk to dump the full MIB.
Confirm UDP 161 is open (nmap -sU -p 161) before brute forcing.

defense.why_it_works: SNMPv1/v2c uses community strings for authentication with no lockout mechanism and no encryption. Strings are sent in cleartext and can be brute forced or sniffed.
defense.prerequisites: UDP port 161 reachable from attacker. SNMP service running on target.
defense.misconfiguration: Default community strings 'public'/'private' left unchanged. No firewall restricting SNMP access to management hosts only.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# snmpd.conf — default read-write access
rocommunity public  default  # read from any host
rwcommunity private default  # write from any host
defense.secure_config:
# snmpd.conf — SNMPv3 only, no v1/v2c
# Remove all rocommunity / rwcommunity lines
createUser adminUser SHA 'StrongPass123!' AES 'StrongPriv456!'
rouser adminUser authPriv .1
# Firewall: only allow UDP 161 from management VLAN
defense.impact: Valid community string provides read (or read-write) access to the full SNMP MIB — OS info, processes, interfaces, routing, installed software.
defense.detection: High rate of SNMP GET requests with different community strings from a single source. SNMP agent logs (where enabled) record invalid community string attempts.
defense.artifacts: Network captures on UDP 161 showing multiple community string attempts. SNMP daemon logs.
defense.prevention: Upgrade to SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption. Block UDP 161 at perimeter firewall. Restrict SNMP to management VLAN with host-based firewall rules. Change default community strings.
defense.evasion: Use correct defaults first (public/private) before brute forcing to minimise noise. Slow request rate to avoid threshold alerts.
